text:
A: Hiya! Oh, it's you, I was hoping I'd get you! I saw your photo and thought, she looks lovely. Sorry, is that weird to say?
B: No! Ah, that's made my day. I'm Nicola. I said the same about yours, I put lovely smile, and I love the dog calendar.
A: Oh, the calendar, yeah, that's Bonnie and Alfie, a different photo every month. I'm Kerry, I'm in Chatham.
B: Chatham! I'm in Eltham, so we're practically neighbours. What are they, your two?
A: Cockapoos. Absolute nightmares, to be fair. They got in the bin again this morning, chicken bones all over the kitchen floor, and I'm thinking, I've got a video call at two, and I'm on my hands and knees with the Dettol...
B: Oh no! Murphy does that. He's a Staffie, he just headbutts the lid till it pops.
A: Aw, a Staffie. They're such softies, aren't they?
B: Big baby. So what do you do, Kerry? I'm guessing hair, with the tunic?
A: Oh, the tunic, yeah, I've come straight from the salon. I manage a little salon in Walderslade, four chairs, and I co-own it with a friend from college. I still do my own clients three days a week, 'cause I'd miss them otherwise, d'you know what I mean? Some of them I've been doing for fifteen years. One of my regulars just had a baby, she sent me a photo this morning, I nearly cried.
B: Oh, that's lovely. That's like me, I'm in a primary school office, front desk, dinner money, all that. I've been there eleven years, so I've seen kids start in Reception and leave in Year Six. You get attached, don't you?
A: You do! And you remember everything about them. I know all my ladies' kids' names, where they're going on holiday, the lot.
B: Same! Steve, my husband, says I'm like a filing cabinet for other people's business. He's an electrician, self-employed, so he's in and out all day.
A: No way, so's my Darren! Self-employed sparky. His van broke down last week and he's been knackered ever since, borrowing his brother's.
B: Oh, the van, it's always the van. Steve's on a job now that he calls a nightmare of old wiring. He comes home and just lies on the settee groaning.
A: That's Darren! Exactly that. Erm, sorry, what d'you do when you're not at work? I'm being nosy now.
B: Ha, no, go on! Book club, dog walks, quiz nights. And Strictly, I'm religious about Strictly.
A: Oh, Strictly, yeah, our family group chat goes mental on a Saturday. And musicals, d'you like a musical?
B: Love a musical. I've seen Mamma Mia three times with my sister.
A: Shut up! Three times, same as me! I go with my sister as well, for birthdays.
B: We're the same person! Do you bake? Please tell me you do a Victoria sponge.
A: I do a Victoria sponge for all the girls' birthdays at the salon!
B: I do one for the school cake sale! This is ridiculous. Where d'you go on holiday then, go on.
A: Erm, all-inclusive, Tenerife or Lanzarote, and we've just booked Tenerife for September. And then caravan weekends, Camber Sands, or Norfolk.
B: Camber! We do a caravan at Camber!
A: Oh my God. Right, we've got to be in the same group chat after this. Is that allowed? Sorry, I don't know if that's allowed.
B: I'm not sure, but I'll risk it. Do you go up the West End much then, for the shows?
A: Birthdays mostly, it's dear, isn't it? But I love it, the whole day, a bit of dinner first, a cocktail...
B: Oh, a cocktail before, yeah, that's the best bit, I always say...
